text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs extended a formal invitation to visit Hungary to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during their meeting yesterday.

- The head of the Prime Minister's cabinet office said the government must honour the parliamentary ruling pertaining to the one percent income tax allocation, despite protests from the Bench of Catholic Bishops, adding that there is little chance that the law be amended in the wake of protests by the Vatican.
- The Pension Insurance Authority yesterday rejected a draft pension reform plan filed by the finance and welfare ministries, ahead of today's all-party consultations on the matter.

- The National Radio and Television Board yesterday approved the final text of a tender pertaining to the operational rights of national commercial television networks, in connection with the planned privatisation of Hungary TV channel 2.

- The Capital Metropolitan Court yesterday ruled that Christian Democratic People's Party President Gyorgy Giczy violated the party's statutes in convening the board session since only the chairman of the board has the right to do so.
- The Young Democrats yesterday called for a parliamentary investigation into the amendment of the Budapest Bank privatisation contract.
- The Free Democrat national council will hold a session on January 25-26.
- The National Bank of Hungary's base rate will drop from 23 percent to 22.5 percent as of January 16.
- A drunken army major fired a pistol at a newspaper photographer in Budapest on Tuesday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz will appeal in a letter within two days to the Russian minister of transport and to the head of the Russian state customs commission, asking them to return 19 Hungarian trucks sequestered two and a half months ago.
- The Russian deputy trade minister will visit Budapest in a few weeks to work out the timetable of setting Russia's $300 million debt to Hungary.
- Yesterday's auction of one-month treasury bills saw a slight increase in the average annual yield, from 21.84 percent last week to 22.07 percent.
- The computer parts manufacturer Intel Corp. introduced their latest processor named MMX Pentium in Budapest yesterday.
- The shares of the pharmceutical firm Human Rt are listed in category A on the stock exchange yesterday.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- A State Privatisation and Holding Co. official yesterday named Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank, GiroCredit, Allianz, Hypo Bank and the Insurer Cuna Mutual Group as the companies that will be invited to submit bids in the closed tender for Takarekbank.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The workers at the MOL oil refinery in Szazhalombatta may go on strike next week if their demands for a 30 percent wage increase are not met.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- MOL is considering the possibility of buying crude oil from Iraq.
- The long-term debts of Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank were upgraded into the investment-grade category by the international credit rating agency Thomson Bankwatch.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
